title: Why do companies see empolyees like this...
description:
Companies see employees as subscriptions—easy to cancel when it suits them. But the lives they disrupt? Mortgages, student loans, and actual livelihoods. 

Why is it easier to cancel a career than it is to cancel Netflix?

transcript: should not take six months to get a job and then just a click of a button to lose it I think companies employers think of us as subscriptions you as an employee are just in a subscription and they're paying you for every month that they're using you and then just like you and I when we're like you know what I need to start saving some money I don't know about you the first thing I do is download one of those apps and then tell me what my subscriptions are and go through and cancel all these subscriptions I'm like oh my god I didn't even know if I was paying for that cancel I'm saving $10 here $20 here I fear that is what companies do when they people off them that is what they think they're just canceling their subscriptions with us instead of it being $10 that they're saving so that way they can get an extra cup of Starbucks this week it is a person's life they're ruining they're literally ruining a livelihood these are people with mortgages and rent and bills and student loans and children unsubscribe that is not cool and there should not be more protections for me to cancel Netflix than there is for employees to not be cancelled at work
